definition: Bertelsmann Music Group's video game arm in the 1990s. It published the first Grand Theft Auto in 1997 and was sold to Take-Two in 1998.
The Dundee studio that made the first Grand Theft Auto and later became Rockstar North.
Rockstar's Scottish studio (Dundee, later Edinburgh), where GTA music and audio were overseen and mastered through the early games.
A New York club night Sam Houser and Terry Donovan started in 1999 with Body & Soul promoter John Davis; it wound down in 2000.
A New York Sunday party; its promoter John Davis partnered on Rockstar Loft, and Andi Hanley was a warm-up DJ there.
Ivan Pavlovich's title at Rockstar, which he joined in 2004; he leads music curation across games and GTA Online updates.
The person who sources and clears licensed tracks for a game; Pavlovich and Andi Hanley held the role on GTA IV.
A short station-branding jingle or voice tag between songs, recorded after a station's tracks are chosen.
Processing every track so all stations sit at the same level and character, as on a real broadcast chain.
Reducing the heavy compression of modern masters so newer tracks sit beside older records on the same station.
All-speech GTA stations of scripted shows, callers and ads, which began in GTA III partly as a way to fill airtime cheaply.
A station picked and hosted by an outside artist, such as Flying Lotus's station in GTA V, built from unreleased music from his friends.
